Bright daylight and long shadows lie across dusty tan earth in a sparse Wild West settlement. The broad, flat expanse is enclosed on three sides by irregular walls of tall, warm sandstone outcrops, leaving the remaining edge open. Generous empty space separates the compact town from the surrounding cliffs.

Roughly eight small wooden frontier buildings stand in two loose, orderly rows facing a wide central dirt street. A dark timber church has a steep roof, narrow arched windows, a fenced yard, and a square bell tower. Several pale clapboard houses and shops with dark framing and pitched roofs share the rows with a few simple boxy sheds and rear structures.

From the open side, a short straight railway approaches the church, carrying a black steam locomotive and tender. Low dark picket fencing wraps much of the developed area, broken for paths and the railway. Telegraph poles stand near the track; scattered barrels and small street props, sparse hitching posts, and two neat groups of weathered period vehicles parked along one outer side complete the dry, quiet, lightly weathered scene.
